sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: marker_equality
tools.description: Compare two marker expressions for equality. left: The left-hand side marker expression to compare, right: The right-hand side marker expression to compare. Example: marker_equality('python_version >= "3.6"', 'python_version >= "3.6"') -> True.

tools.name: marker_inequality
tools.description:
The `!=` operator with Marker objects, as in `left != right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `!=`, never as a call of `__ne__`. At least one side is a Marker object.
    
    Example: marker_inequality('python_version >= "3.6"', 'python_version < "3.6"') -> True

tools.name: marker_intersection
tools.description: Combine two marker expressions with logical AND. left: The left-hand side marker expression, right: The right-hand side marker expression. Example: marker_intersection('python_version >= "3.6"', 'os_name == "posix"') -> 'python_version >= "3.6" and os_name == "posix"'.

tools.name: marker_union
tools.description: Combine two marker expressions with logical OR. left: The left-hand side marker expression, right: The right-hand side marker expression. Example: marker_union('python_version >= "3.6"', 'sys_platform == "win32"') -> 'python_version >= "3.6" or sys_platform == "win32"'.

tools.name: evaluate_marker
tools.description: Evaluate a marker expression against an environment. marker: A marker expression to evaluate, e.g. 'python_version >= "3.6"' -> True. environment: Mapping containing keys and values to override the detected environment. context: The context in which the marker is evaluated, which influences what marker names are considered valid. Accepted values are "metadata" (default), "lock_file", and "requirement".

tools.name: create_empty_version_range
tools.description: Create an empty version range that accepts no versions. prereleases: whether prereleases should be considered when checking version inclusion -> the created empty version range.

tools.name: create_full_version_range
tools.description: Create a full version range that accepts all versions. admit_arbitrary: whether to admit arbitrary strings as versions; prereleases: whether to include pre-release versions.

tools.name: create_singleton_version_range
tools.description: Create a version range that contains only a single version. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string, e.g. '1.0' -> '{1.0}'. prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions; if None, uses the default behavior.

tools.name: intersect_version_ranges
tools.description: Compute the intersection of two version ranges. range1: First version range specifier, range2: Second version range specifier. Example: intersect_version_ranges(">=1.0", "<2.0") -> ">=1.0,<2.0".

tools.name: union_version_ranges
tools.description: Compute the union of two version ranges. version_range_a: First version range in PEP 440 format. version_range_b: Second version range in PEP 440 format. Example: union_version_ranges(">=1.0", "<2.0") -> ">=1.0,<2.0".

tools.name: complement_version_range
tools.description: Compute the complement of a version range. version_range: A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet, e.g. '>=1.0' -> '<1.0'.

tools.name: check_version_range_subset
tools.description: Check if one version range is a subset of another. range1: First version range specifier, range2: Second version range specifier to check if range1 is a subset of this. >>> check_version_range_subset('>=1.5,<1.8', '>=1.0,<2.0') -> True

tools.name: check_version_range_superset
tools.description: Check if one version range is a superset of another. outer_range: A version range specifier string for the outer range. inner_range: A version range specifier string for the inner range. >>> check_version_range_superset('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=1.5,<1.8') True

tools.name: check_version_ranges_disjoint
tools.description: Check if two version ranges are disjoint. range1: First version range specifier, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0'. range2: Second version range specifier, e.g. '>=2.0,<3.0'. -> True if ranges don't overlap, False otherwise.

tools.name: check_version_in_range
tools.description:
Check if a version is contained in a version range.
    
    :param version_range: A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
    :param version: The version string to check against the range
    :return: True if the version is contained in the range, False otherwise
    
    >>> check_version_in_range(">=1.0,<2.0", "1.5")
    True
    >>> check_version_in_range(">=1.0,<2.0", "2.0")
    False

tools.name: convert_range_to_specifier_set
tools.description: Convert a version range to a specifier set. specifier_set: A specifier set string that can be parsed into a SpecifierSet, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> '<2.0,>=1.0'.

tools.name: specifier_equality
tools.description:
The `==` operator with Specifier objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a Specifier object.
    
    Example: specifier_equality(">=1.0", ">=1.0") -> True

tools.name: specifier_inequality
tools.description:
The `!=` operator with Specifier objects, as in `left != right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `!=`, never as a call of `__ne__`. At least one side is a Specifier object.
    
    Example: specifier_inequality(">=1.0", "<2.0") -> True

tools.name: version_in_specifier
tools.description: Check if a version is contained within a specifier. version: A version string to check against the specifier, e.g. '1.2.3' -> true for specifier '>=1.0'. specifier: A version specifier string (e.g., '>=1.0', '==1.2.3').

tools.name: specifier_set_equality
tools.description:
The `==` operator with SpecifierSet objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a SpecifierSet object.
    
    Example: specifier_set_equality('>=3.0', '>=3.0') -> True

tools.name: specifier_set_inequality
tools.description:
The `!=` operator with SpecifierSet objects, as in `left != right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `!=`, never as a call of `__ne__`. At least one side is a SpecifierSet object.
    
    Example: specifier_set_inequality(">=1.0", "<2.0") -> True

tools.name: version_in_specifier_set
tools.description: Check if a version is contained within a specifier set. version: A version string to check against the specifier set, e.g. '3.2' specifier_set: A string representation of a version specifier set, e.g. '>=3.0,!=3.1' -> true.

tools.name: specifier_set_intersection
tools.description: Combine two specifier sets with logical AND. left: A string representation of the left specifier set, right: A string representation of the right specifier set. Example: specifier_set_intersection('>=1.0,<2.0', '<1.5') -> '>=1.0,<1.5'.

tools.name: check_specifier_set_unsatisfiable
tools.description:
Check whether this specifier set can never be satisfied.
    
    Returns True if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously.
    
    Args:
        specifiers (str): A string representation of version specifiers
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the specifier set is unsatisfiable, False otherwise
        
    Example:
        >>> check_specifier_set_unsatisfiable(">=2.0,<1.0")
        True

tools.name: convert_specifier_set_to_range
tools.description: Convert a specifier set to a version range. specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'.

tools.name: check_specifier_set_subset
tools.description: Check if one specifier set is a subset of another. specifier_set1: The first specifier set to check. specifier_set2: The second specifier set to check against. >>> check_specifier_set_subset('>=3.12,<3.13', '>=3.12') True

tools.name: check_specifier_set_superset
tools.description: Check if one specifier set is a superset of another. specifier_set1: The first specifier set to check. specifier_set2: The second specifier set to check. >>> check_specifier_set_superset('>=3.12', '>=3.12,<3.13') True

tools.name: check_specifier_sets_disjoint
tools.description: Check if two specifier sets are disjoint. specifier_set1: First specifier set string, specifier_set2: Second specifier set string. >>> check_specifier_sets_disjoint('<3.12', '>=3.12') True

tools.name: check_version_in_specifier_set
tools.description: Check if a version is contained in a specifier set. specifier_set: A string representing the version specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1'), version: The version string to check against the specifier set, prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this SpecifierSet. If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440.

tools.name: filter_versions_by_specifier_set
tools.description:
Filter a list of versions based on a specifier set.
    
    :param specifiers: A string representing version specifiers (e.g., '>=1.2.3')
    :param versions: List of version strings or objects to filter
    :param prereleases: Whether to include prerelease versions
    
    >>> filter_versions_by_specifier_set(">=1.2.3", ["1.2", "1.3", "1.5a1"])
    ['1.3']

tools.name: tag_equality
tools.description:
The `==` operator with Tag objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a Tag object.
    
    Example:
    >>> tag1 = Tag('cp39', 'cp39m', 'linux_x86_64')
    >>> tag2 = Tag('cp39', 'cp39m', 'linux_x86_64')
    >>> tag_equality(tag1, tag2)
    True
tools.direct_call: packaging.tags.Tag(left['interpreter'], left['abi'], left['platform']) == packaging.tags.Tag(right['interpreter'], right['abi'], right['platform'])

tools.name: version_less_than
tools.description: Check if one version is less than another. version1: The first version string to compare, version2: The second version string to compare.

tools.name: version_less_equal
tools.description: Check if one version is less than or equal to another. left: The left-hand version string to compare, right: The right-hand version string to compare.

tools.name: version_greater_than
tools.description: Check if one version is greater than another. left_version: The left-hand version string to compare, right_version: The right-hand version string to compare.

tools.name: version_greater_equal
tools.description: Check if one version is greater than or equal to another. version1: The first version string to compare, version2: The second version string to compare.

tools.name: version_equality
tools.description:
The `==` operator with Version objects, as in `left == right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `==`, never as a call of `__eq__`. At least one side is a Version object.
    
    Example: version_equality("1.0", "1.0") -> True

tools.name: version_inequality
tools.description:
The `!=` operator with Version objects, as in `left != right`. It is an operator, not a function: use it as an expression with `!=`, never as a call of `__ne__`. At least one side is a Version object.
    
    Example: version_inequality("1.0", "1.1") -> True

tools.name: get_version_epoch
tools.description:
Get the epoch component of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the epoch from -> The epoch of the version.
    
    >>> get_version_epoch("2.0.0")
    0
    >>> get_version_epoch("1!2.0.0")
    1

tools.name: get_version_release
tools.description: Get the release component of a version. version: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.2.3' -> [1, 2, 3].

tools.name: get_version_pre
tools.description: Get the pre-release component of a version. version: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.2.3a1' -> ('a', 1).

tools.name: get_version_post
tools.description:
Get the post-release component of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the post-release component from
    
    >>> print(Version("1.2.3").post)
    None
    >>> Version("1.2.3.post1").post
    1

tools.name: get_version_dev
tools.description: Get the development component of a version. version: A version string to parse -> The development number or None.

tools.name: get_version_local
tools.description: Get the local version segment of the version. version: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.2.3+abc' -> 'abc'.

tools.name: get_version_public
tools.description: Get the public portion of a version. version: A version string to extract the public portion from -> e.g. '1.2.3+abc' -> '1.2.3'.

tools.name: get_version_base
tools.description:
Get the base version of a version. version: A version string to extract the base version from -> The base version string.
    
    >>> get_version_base("1.2.3")
    '1.2.3'
    >>> get_version_base("1.2.3+abc")
    '1.2.3'
    >>> get_version_base("1!1.2.3dev1+abc")
    '1!1.2.3'
